message.content:
Build a **flagship marketing showcase page** for **Nxeon Matrix** — the most engaging, animated, conversion-focused page on the Nxeon marketing site (/opt/nxeon, Next.js App Router). Add a "Matrix" entry to the marketing nav and create the page at **`app/matrix/page.tsx`**.

## What Nxeon Matrix IS (the pitch — use real, specific copy, no lorem)
Matrix is Nxeon's flagship AI app builder: **open several AI build consoles at once and build multiple apps in parallel — on your own servers.** Key points to sell:
- **Parallel multi-console workspace** — 1–6 live consoles, each building a different project (or the same prompt mirrored across several servers at once).
- **Two ways to build, your choice per console:** use your own **Anthropic API key**, OR run the **Claude CLI that's pre-installed on your VPS** using your **Claude Pro/Max subscription** — a real terminal, right in the browser. (Cost angle worth making: a whole site/app is often a few dollars of API, or unlimited on a flat subscription.)
- **Project pipelines / planners** and a build board that tracks each project's real status.
- **From idea to live app in minutes** — describe what you want, approve the plan, and it configures your server. Great for shipping a **SaaS product, an API, a Discord bot, a landing page, automations** — build it, run it, make money.
- It runs on infrastructure the customer already has with Nxeon — no local setup, no laptop, build from anywhere.

## Honor the existing marketing design system (do NOT invent a clashing look)
READ these first and match them exactly — this page must feel like the same product:
- `components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx` (the nav — ADD a "Matrix" link here), `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx`.
- `components/marketing/primitives.tsx`, `components/marketing/sections.tsx`, `components/marketing/Reveal.tsx` (scroll-reveal animation helper — reuse it).
- An existing marketing page for structure/metadata/JSON-LD conventions (e.g. `app/vps/page.tsx`, `app/security/page.tsx`, or `app/vibe-coding/page.tsx` — read whichever exist). Reuse the site's brand tokens (brand-* colors, gradients), section rhythm, `PageHeader`/section primitives, and SEO metadata pattern (export `metadata`, add JSON-LD if other pages do). If there's a sitemap list (`app/sitemap.ts`), add `/matrix`.

## Make it the most engaging page on the site
This is the flagship — spend real craft here, but stay on-brand and tasteful (not AI-slop). Ideas (choose what lands; you own the art direction):
- **Hero: an animated "matrix" of build consoles** — a grid of small console panes that light up / type prompts / stream a build in sequence, evoking many projects building at once. Canvas or CSS animation; keep it smooth and GPU-friendly.
- A **live-feeling console mockup** that types a prompt → shows a plan → "builds" (staged, faux but believable) — the "watch it build" moment.
- **Scroll-triggered reveals** (use the existing `Reveal`), section-by-section: how it works (open consoles → describe → build across servers), the dual-mode split (your key ⟷ your server's Claude), a parallel-builds showcase, use-case cards (SaaS / API / bot / site / automation), a stat/social-proof strip, and a strong final CTA ("Start building" → the app / signup).
- Tasteful **micro-interactions** (hover, glow on the neon accent), device/screen framing for the mockups, a cohesive neon-on-dark aesthetic consistent with the Nxeon brand.
- **Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`** (gate the heavy animation). Theme-aware if the rest of the marketing site is. Keyboard-accessible; visible focus.

## Rules
- Self-contained page + any new components under `components/marketing/matrix/**`. Inline/CSS/Canvas animation preferred over heavy new deps (nothing new in package.json).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for your files. It must build — no client-only APIs at module scope in a server component (mark interactive/animated pieces `"use client"`). Wide content scrolls inside its own container; body never scrolls sideways; responsive down to mobile.
- Real, benefit-led copy. Active voice. A CTA says exactly what happens.
- Add the "Matrix" nav link in `MarketingHeader.tsx` (match the existing link style/placement).
- Do NOT run next build in place, git commit, deploy, or systemctl. I integrate + build centrally.

## Deliver
Typechecking page + components + the nav link. Final report: files created/changed, where you added the nav link, what animations/effects you used and how you gated reduced-motion, whether you added to the sitemap, and any new component files. Report is data for me, not a user message.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

I'm building the ConsoleMatrix component as a grid of six console panes that animate in sequence, each displaying a project name, accent color, and a series of typed prompts and build output. A frame-based system advances every ~130ms, with each pane's progress offset by its index to create a cascading effect—they cycle through their scripts, show live output, then restart the sequence.

For the animation mechanics, I'm tracking a global tick that increments every 120ms, and each pane maps its local tick (adjusted by an offset) into a looping timeline. The timeline progressively reveals lines from the script, with the current line showing character-by-character typing for realism, and once all lines are revealed, a green "LIVE" pill appears with a glow effect before the cycle repeats.

To keep rendering efficient, I'm precomputing a flat array of frames for each script at module load—each frame captures the full visible text state including the typing progress and caret position. This way the render just indexes into a precomputed array based on the current tick, avoiding expensive calculations every frame.

All checks pass. Here is my final report.

## Summary

Built the flagship **Nxeon Matrix** marketing showcase page, matching the existing marketing design system (brand-* tokens, `Section`/`SectionTitle`/`Eyebrow` primitives, `Reveal`, `card`/`card-hover`, `grad-text`, `hero-aura`, `btn-primary/secondary`, `eyebrow-pill`, tone bands). Copy is real and product-accurate — grounded in the actual app (`WORKSPACE_NAME = "Matrix"`, `MAX_CONSOLES = 6`, mirror mode 2–6, app route `/dashboard/build`).

### Files created
- **`app/(marketing)/matrix/page.tsx`** — the page (server component). Note: placed under the `(marketing)` route group (URL is still `/matrix`) so it inherits the marketing header/footer chrome, consistent with every other marketing page (`vibe-coding`, `vps`, etc.). Exports `metadata` (title/description/canonical/openGraph, same pattern as other pages) and renders `FaqJsonLd` for SEO rich results. Sections: animated hero, How it works (open consoles → describe → build across servers), Watch it build, dual-mode split (your key ⟷ your server's Claude), parallel-builds showcase, use-case cards (SaaS/API/bot/site/automation/internal tool), animated stat strip, FAQ, and a strong final CTA.
- **`components/marketing/matrix/ConsoleMatrix.tsx`** — hero visual: a 6-pane grid of build consoles that type prompts, stream builds, and cascade to "LIVE".
- **`components/marketing/matrix/LiveBuildConsole.tsx`** — the "watch it build" console (types prompt → plan → staged build + progress bar → live), with an interactive, keyboard-accessible **dual-mode segmented toggle** (Your API key ⟷ Your server's Claude) using `aria-pressed` and visible focus rings.
- **`components/marketing/matrix/BuildBoard.tsx`** — parallel-builds status board; rows advance Queued → Planning → Building → Live.
- **`components/marketing/matrix/useReducedMotion.ts`** — shared SSR-safe reduced-motion hook.

### Files changed
- **`components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx`** — nav link added in two places: a **top-level desktop link** "Matrix" between Compare-adjacent items (`<TopLink href="/matrix">`, right after the Products trigger, before Pricing), and a **Products mega-menu item** under the "Compute" group (with a "New" badge, `IconApps`), which also surfaces it in the mobile drawer. Imported `IconApps`.
- **`app/sitemap.ts`** — added `{ path: "/matrix", priority: 0.9, freq: "monthly" }`.

### Animations & reduced-motion gating
All three animated components are driven by a single `setInterval` frame counter, with each frame's visuals derived as a **pure function** of that counter from precomputed timelines (no per-element timers, cheap re-renders, GPU-friendly CSS transitions for glow/width). Effects: character-by-character prompt typing, staged build-line streaming, growing progress bars, cascading "LIVE" glow rings, blinking carets (reusing the existing `animate-blink` keyframe), and count-up stats via the existing `StatCounter`. **Reduced motion** is honored via `useReducedMotion` — when set, the interval never starts and each component is pinned to its finished resting frame (all consoles "LIVE", board all "Live", progress 100%), so reduced-motion visitors see a static, complete state with zero motion. `StatCounter` already respects the preference internally. The mode toggle remains fully interactive regardless.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — **0 errors** project-wide.
- No new dependencies (nothing touched in `package.json`); all animation is inline React state + existing CSS keyframes.
- Wide console content scrolls/clips inside its own bordered container; grid is responsive (2-col → 3-col), body never scrolls sideways.

I did not run `next build`, git, deploy, or systemctl, per your instructions.
